plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled flowers on bare branches in late winter. It is widely cultivated in East Asia for ornament and for its fruit, which is used in pickles and liqueur.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in East Asia as a symbol of perseverance because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground, often before cherry blossoms.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes through frost and snow and naturalizes in woodlands and gardens.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used for symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with the largest flower head of any protea, a bowl-shaped cluster of pink bracts surrounding a center of silky, hair-tipped florets. It grows in fynbos vegetation and is the national flower of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early summer depending on altitude, with peak flowering from late winter through spring in some populations; some blooms are present in February
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the most ancient flowering plants, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and in woodland gardens with acidic soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Japan, Korea, China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea, and thousands of cultivars have been bred.
